source: KWS Academy Professional Discovery Assessment Master Specification (Parts A-D). Text is copied verbatim; do not edit.

questions.text: Imagine a group has just come up with an exciting new idea. Before the group decides what to do, what would you be most inclined to contribute?

options.text: Explore how the idea could become something valuable or create an opportunity.
Think of something creative that could bring the idea to life.
Find people who could contribute and bring everyone together.
Organize the work and make sure things move forward.

questions.text: You have one month to work on a personal project that could help your professional growth. Which part would excite you most?

options.text: Finding people to collaborate with, learn from or involve in the project.
Exploring how the project could create value, attract interest or open up opportunities.
Researching the subject, understanding the problem and deciding the best approach.
Organizing the work, setting milestones and making sure I complete it.

questions.text: You're attending an event where professionals from different parts of the media, marketing and communications industries are sharing their experiences. What would make the event most worthwhile to you?

options.text: Discovering new creative ideas, tools and ways of producing work.
Understanding how people turn their skills, ideas and services into business opportunities.
Learning how projects are organized, managed and delivered successfully.
Learning about industry trends, changes and where the industry is heading.

questions.text: A team has worked on a campaign, but the results are disappointing. What would you be most interested in looking into?

options.text: Whether the right people were involved and communication was effective.
Whether the message was clear and connected with the intended audience.
Whether the product, service or offer gave people a compelling reason to respond.
Whether the creative work was engaging and effective.

questions.text: A community event is being organized. The purpose and overall direction have already been agreed upon. Which part would you most enjoy taking responsibility for?

options.text: Organizing activities, managing responsibilities and ensuring the event is delivered.
Shaping the message and deciding how the event should communicate its ideas.
Building relationships, coordinating people and encouraging collaboration.
Developing the creative work and bringing concepts to life.

questions.text: A friend has a good product but is struggling to attract customers. Where would your attention naturally go first?

options.text: Identifying people or networks that could help the product reach more customers.
Understanding the customers, the market and how the product should be positioned.
Exploring how the product could be packaged, priced or presented to create greater value.
Finding the best way to describe the product and communicate why people should care.

questions.text: Two people on a team disagree about the direction of a project. What would you naturally contribute?

options.text: Examining their arguments against the project's objective and identifying the strongest direction.
Turning the agreed direction into clear responsibilities and next steps.
Helping them explain their positions clearly and understand one another.
Bringing them into a constructive conversation and helping them find common ground.

questions.text: You have an exciting idea, but you don't have much money, equipment or support. What are you most likely to do?

options.text: Create a small sample or prototype to demonstrate what the idea could become.
Find a compelling way to explain the idea and attract people's interest.
Test whether people would be interested in it and whether it could become a viable opportunity.
Evaluate the idea carefully and identify the most practical way forward.

questions.text: Imagine you notice that people around you are struggling with a problem, but nobody seems to be addressing it. What would you most naturally want to do?

options.text: Organize a practical way to address the problem and ensure something gets done.
Think of something useful or creative that could help solve the problem.
Find a way to communicate the problem so people understand why it matters.
Understand why the problem exists and identify the most effective way to address it.

questions.text: Which statement best describes your current professional situation?

options.text: I'm still exploring my interests and trying to understand what professional direction may suit me.
I've identified an area of interest and I'm learning the knowledge or skills I need to enter it.
I'm beginning to use what I've learned through projects, assignments, work or personal initiatives.
I'm working in my chosen area and building experience, credibility or a track record.
I'm established in my area and looking to expand my expertise, responsibilities or opportunities.

questions.text: How would you describe your current knowledge and skills in the area you want to grow?

options.text: I'm still discovering my interests and the skills I may want to develop.
I'm learning the fundamentals and building an initial understanding.
I've acquired some knowledge and can apply parts of what I've learned.
I've developed relevant skills and can demonstrate them through completed work or experience.
I have substantial knowledge and experience, and can consistently deliver results.

questions.text: Which statement best describes your practical experience in your chosen or intended area?

options.text: I haven't applied it practically yet; I'm still exploring.
I'm learning, but I have had little opportunity to practise.
I've practised through personal, academic or collaborative work.
I've independently completed projects, handled responsibilities or worked on real assignments.
I've repeatedly applied my capabilities in professional settings and have a track record of completed work.

questions.text: How would you describe your professional visibility and credibility?

options.text: I'm still figuring out how I want to position myself professionally.
I'm beginning to develop a professional identity and present myself in my chosen area.
I've started sharing my work, making connections or creating evidence of what I can do.
I have a portfolio, professional relationships or a track record that demonstrates my work.
I'm recognized for my work or expertise and regularly attract relevant opportunities.

questions.text: What is the biggest thing currently holding back your professional growth?

options.text: I'm unclear about my direction, interests or strengths.
I lack some of the knowledge or skills I need.
I don't have enough opportunities to practise or gain real experience.
I struggle to demonstrate my abilities, build credibility or attract opportunities.
I need stronger connections, guidance, resources or access.
I know what I want to achieve but struggle with consistency, execution or follow-through.
I'm not significantly held back; I'm looking for ways to grow further.

questions.text: What would meaningful progress look like for you over the next 12 months?

options.text: Gaining clarity about my professional direction and the opportunities available to me.
Acquiring knowledge and developing capabilities relevant to my goals.
Completing practical projects and gaining experience I can demonstrate.
Building a stronger portfolio, professional identity and network.
Securing better opportunities, taking on greater responsibilities or growing my professional or business activity.
Expanding my expertise, influence or capacity to create professional or commercial value.

understanding.text: Imagine you're interested in building a career in media, marketing or communications, but you're not sure which direction to take. What would give you the most useful starting point?

options.text: Explore the tools and software commonly used by professionals in the industry.
Look at the most popular career paths and identify the ones attracting attention.
Understand the different industry areas, professional roles, workflows and how they connect.
Start producing work in an area that interests you and learn from the experience.

experience.text: How much experience do you have exploring or understanding the media, marketing and communications industries, their professional roles, platforms and developments?

options.text: I have little or no experience in this area.
I'm beginning to learn about the industry and its different areas.
I've explored the industry through research, courses or personal learning.
I've used my industry knowledge to guide decisions or activities in projects or work.
I regularly apply industry knowledge in professional work and can demonstrate my understanding.

understanding.text: A business has been promoting its products on social media, but it isn't attracting the customers it wants. Before recommending a new marketing approach, what would be most useful to understand?

options.text: Which platforms competitors use and how frequently they publish content.
Which types of content currently receive the most engagement across social media.
Which advertising formats are available and how much each one costs.
Who the business wants to reach, what those customers value and how the offering meets their needs.

experience.text: How much experience do you have developing or applying marketing and brand strategies, understanding audiences, positioning products or planning marketing activities?

options.text: I have little or no experience in this area.
I'm currently learning about marketing and brand strategy.
I've applied some of these ideas in personal, academic or collaborative projects.
I've independently applied marketing or brand strategy to real projects or businesses.
I've repeatedly developed or applied strategies, evaluated performance and improved outcomes.

understanding.text: An organization wants young people to understand a new initiative and take part in it. What should guide the way its message is developed?

options.text: The communication style and language that have worked well for similar organizations.
The audience's interests, the purpose of the message and what the organization wants people to understand or do.
The communication channels with the largest audiences and the formats that attract the most attention.
The amount of information the organization needs to share and how it can all fit into one message.

experience.text: How much experience do you have developing messages, writing content, shaping stories or communicating ideas to specific audiences?

options.text: I have little or no experience in this area.
I'm currently learning how to communicate ideas and develop content.
I've created content, written or communicated ideas through personal, academic or collaborative work.
I've independently developed communication materials, content or stories for real projects or audiences.
I've consistently developed and delivered communication or storytelling projects and can demonstrate their effectiveness.

understanding.text: A team needs to produce a short video campaign for a particular audience. What should it consider when deciding how the video will be created?

options.text: The equipment available and the production techniques the team can use confidently.
The visual style of successful videos in the same industry and how to achieve a similar result.
The amount of footage required and the editing techniques that will make the video engaging.
The video's purpose, intended audience, platform, format and available production resources.

experience.text: How much experience do you have planning or producing digital content such as photography, videos, graphics, audio or other media?

options.text: I have little or no experience in this area.
I'm learning about content creation and media production.
I've created content through personal, academic or collaborative projects.
I've independently planned or produced content for real projects, businesses or audiences.
I regularly produce professional content and can demonstrate my work and production experience.

understanding.text: An organization has agreed on a campaign strategy and wants to launch in three weeks. What would be the most useful next step before execution begins?

options.text: Break the campaign into activities, assign responsibilities, establish timelines and identify the resources required.
Begin developing the campaign's promotional materials so the team has something ready to publish.
Bring everyone together to discuss the campaign and allow team members to decide how they will contribute.
Establish the campaign's performance targets and decide how its results will be measured.

experience.text: How much experience do you have planning, coordinating or executing projects, events, campaigns or organized initiatives?

options.text: I have little or no experience in this area.
I've participated in projects but have had limited planning or coordination responsibilities.
I've organized or executed personal, academic, volunteer or collaborative initiatives.
I've independently planned or coordinated real projects, managing responsibilities and timelines.
I've repeatedly managed projects or campaigns from planning through delivery and evaluation.

understanding.text: A photographer has strong technical skills and produces good work but struggles to attract paying clients consistently. What would be most useful to address?

options.text: Improving the quality of equipment and investing in more advanced photography techniques.
Increasing social media activity and publishing more examples of completed work.
Identifying a suitable customer group, understanding its needs and developing an offering with clear value and pricing.
Studying successful photographers and adopting the promotional strategies they use.

experience.text: How much experience do you have positioning yourself professionally, building a portfolio, developing professional relationships or turning your skills into business opportunities?

options.text: I have little or no experience in this area.
I've started exploring professional development and how to present my work.
I've taken some steps through personal branding, networking, portfolio development or offering services.
I've independently positioned my skills, built professional relationships or pursued clients and opportunities.
I've consistently applied these skills to build a reputation, secure opportunities or generate business value.

questions.text: Which of these best describes your current situation?

options.text: I'm currently a university or college student.
I've recently graduated and I'm preparing to enter the professional world.
I'm exploring a career in media, marketing or communications.
I'm already working in one of these industries and want to develop further.
I'm a content creator or digital creative looking to strengthen my professional capabilities.
I'm an entrepreneur or business owner looking to improve how I use media and marketing in my business.
I'm a freelancer or independent creative professional.
Other.

questions.text: What is the biggest challenge currently limiting your professional growth?

options.text: I'm not sure which professional direction to pursue.
I lack some of the knowledge or skills required to progress.
I understand what I need to do but lack practical experience.
I struggle to demonstrate my abilities through a strong portfolio or track record.
I find it difficult to attract opportunities, clients or professional connections.
I need better guidance, mentorship or accountability.
I have several of these challenges.
I am not currently facing a major challenge; I want to improve and advance.

questions.text: How important is it for you to address this challenge?

options.text: It's not a major priority right now.
It's something I'd like to address within the next 6–12 months.
It's important, and I want to make progress within the next 3–6 months.
It's a high priority, and I want to take action within the next 1–3 months.
I need to address it as soon as possible.

questions.text: KWS Academy's Professional Development Programme is an in-person, 10-week programme in Ikeja, Lagos. How accessible would attending be for you?

options.text: I'm based in Lagos and can attend comfortably.
I'm outside Lagos but can travel or arrange accommodation.
I could attend if the schedule and logistics are manageable.
I would need a different location or delivery format.
Attending in person would not currently be possible.

questions.text: The KWS Academy Professional Development Programme is a 10-week experience with a programme fee of ₦1,200,000. How would you describe your current financial readiness for an investment of this size?

options.text: I can comfortably make this investment.
I can make this investment with some financial planning.
I may be able to make this investment with support or an alternative payment arrangement.
I am interested, but this is currently beyond my financial capacity.
I am not currently considering a paid programme at this investment level.

questions.text: The next Professional Development Programme cohort is scheduled for January 2027. How likely are you to consider joining?

options.text: I'm ready and seriously considering joining the January cohort.
I'm interested and would like to understand the programme better before deciding.
I would like to join, but I need more time to prepare.
I am interested in a future cohort instead.
I'm not currently considering joining.

questions.text: Your Next Step. You've completed your Professional Discovery Journey and gained some insight into your professional style, growth stage and development areas. Would you like to have a conversation with a member of the KWS Academy team to gain further clarity on your results, discuss your professional goals and explore possible next steps?

options.text: Yes, I'd like to schedule a consultation.
I'd like to, but I'd prefer to receive more information first.
Not at the moment. I'm happy with my assessment results for now.

questions.text: Where did you first hear about this Professional Discovery Journey?

options.text: Instagram
Facebook
LinkedIn
WhatsApp
TikTok
A friend, colleague or personal referral
KWS Academy or DreamLife Studios
Other.

conditional.text: Which institution do you currently attend or did you graduate from?

scoring.partB: Q1-Q4: A=1,B=2,C=3,D=4,E=5; mean rounded to nearest whole stage; Q5 and Q6 not scored; flag MIXED-STAGE when max minus min >= 2

partC.understanding: 1 point if the selected key equals correctUnderstandingKey, else 0 (INTERNAL, never shown to the respondent)
partC.note: keep understanding and experience separate; no combined score
